callerReachability: WorkspaceStore.read normalizes storage.local copies into fresh plain store/member objects. normalizeEntry emits validated string URLs and IDs; normalizeStore removes duplicate IDs and emits dense arrays. normalizeMembers emits plain records and quarantine arrays.

WorkspaceStore.reconcile runs inside locked transact, normalizes each operation, rolls session, then synchronously reconciles browser tabs and returns a structuredClone(store). No callback awaits inside matching. Native API tabs are data snapshots; no user-defined getters are installed in inspected caller.

Actual other public helper caller is adoptPinned at workspace.js:1369, not a function named adoptTabsInSpace. It calls findEntriesByUrl inside workspace.update/mutate then filters for null favorite space or requested space; it may add entries between sequential helper calls. Public helper B stays byte-identical and no cross-call cache exists.

Getter/exclude callback/proxy/reentrant fixtures are valid exported-function JavaScript inputs; stored accessors are removed by normalization/cloning. Saved-store mutation via tab.url getters and excluded throwing URLs is not reachable through inspected application callers, but is observably different at the exported reconcile boundary.

Raw duplicate IDs and URLs are still covered without normalization in corpus. indexNodes remains byte-identical, including favorite null and last duplicate ID ownership. Dynamic boundEntries filtering occurs on every B lookup, including after previous-session claims following bucket creation.

retention.scope: 42 separate local Node processes; forced-GC V8 heap at before/second-pending-tab/after-return. Includes whole reconcile state and probe perturbation. After-return GC follows a new event-loop task to clear WeakRef keep-alive. Not peak physical RAM or whole-browser memory. Structural counts are logical live bucket ownership, not physical allocations.
retention.limitations: Two-tab intermediate observation is live state, not a measured peak bound. Forced GC and Map WeakRef instrumentation perturb heap. After-return observation uses a new event-loop task; no index is persistently cached. Repeated isolated process phases are V8 heap evidence only; browser peak/RSS and realistic live memory acceptance remain pending.
retention.exploratory: Original same-job after-return WeakRef probe retained in retention-exploratory.json and excluded from release-after-return inference.
